title: Budgeted-token admission with tiered-fidelity fallbacks and regional failover orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: During recent multi-region spikes we observed tail-latency and error-rate regressions when a single region's allocator became saturated. Pure token-based rate limits are too coarse: high-value short requests get rejected alongside long low-priority streams. Goal: implement a budgeted-token admission controller that enforces per-tenant and per-route token credits with progressive fidelity fallbacks (e.g., candidate pruning, output sampling, shorter max tokens, and model-variant fallback) and integrates with regional failover/circuit-breaker signals so that shedding decisions can be made region-aware and proportionally across replicas.
updates: 2026-02-26 - Ticket created; initial problem statement and broad solution sketch. Assigned to Marcus Li.
2026-03-01 - Design sync with Runtime and Routing teams. Decided to keep budgeting in the front-door admission layer (proxy) to avoid touching kernel-level runtime admission for initial rollout.

2026-03-03 - Prototype of per-tenant sliding token-window credit allocator completed (benchmarked with synthetic mix). Observed ~12% reduction in P95 latency under overload when prefixed with candidate pruning.

2026-03-06 - Reviewed with PM/Console team: will surface per-tenant budget usage in Console and add toggle for progressive fidelity features. PM requested user-facing docs and an opt-out for enterprise customers.

2026-03-09 - Integration test wiring to multi-region health scoreboard and circuit-breaker proof-of-concept. Added GitHub draft PR for admission service and a feature-flag gate. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128
2026-03-10 - Started writing rollout playbook and observability dashboards; added acceptance criteria. Planning canary in us-west2 with 5% traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant and per-route token budgets enforced in proxy layer with bounded memory overhead (<1MB per 10k tenants)
Progressive fidelity toggle sequence implemented and configurable per-tenant: [candidate-prune, max-tokens-reduce, response-sampling, model-variant-fallback]
Regional circuit-breaker signals are consumed to adjust local budgets within 5s of threshold crossing
Canary in us-west2 (5% traffic) shows no customer-facing errors for high-priority tenants and reduces P95 latency by >=10% under synthetic overload compared to baseline
Console surfaces per-tenant budget usage, recent shedding events, and an override toggle for enterprise tenants
Automatic fallback triggers preserve SLOs for P0 tenants (as defined in tenant metadata) while shedding lower-priority traffic
proposed_solution: Introduce a small admission microservice that maintains sliding-window token credits at two dimensions: tenant and route. Credits are debited at request ingress based on estimated token consumption (prompt length + expected generation). When budgets are insufficient, the admission service steps through configured fidelity reducers in-order. The admission service subscribes to the regional health scoreboard and an existing circuit-breaker stream; when a region degrades, the service proportionally reduces local budgets and increases probability of early fidelity steps. Decisions are logged and emitted as events to Kafka for Console and incident analysis.
design_notes: Use leaky-bucket-like sliding window (token credits increment per-second) to smooth bursts instead of strict token buckets
Estimate generation token cost using recent model-seen distribution; allow per-model overrides for accuracy
Fidelity reducers must be idempotent and cheap: e.g., deterministic candidate pruning, clamp max_output_tokens, then model swap to smaller quantized variant
Expose per-tenant policy via Console with admin override; default conservative policy applied to free-tier tenants
Admission microservice to be implemented in Go, colocated with edge proxies for <1ms median extra hop
Telemetry: emit 'admission.decisions' with keys: tenant_id, route, decision_step, estimated_tokens, region, reason
test_plan: Unit tests for budget accounting and fidelity step ordering
Integration test with runtime's model-variant switcher to validate safe model fallback
Chaos test: simulate region node loss and verify budgets adapt across regions without global outage
Load test with mixed tenants (P0/P1/P2) and synthetic long-tail requests to measure P95/P99 improvement
End-to-end canary: enable for 5% traffic in us-west2 and monitor SLOs for 48h
rollout_plan: Canary (5%) us-west2 for 48h with read-only Console visibility
Expand to 25% across us-west2 + us-central for 72h if metrics look stable
Default-on for new accounts after 2-week observation; enterprise tenants kept opt-out until SLA review
rollback_plan: Flip feature-flag off (global) — admission decisions revert to existing token limits
If off toggle doesn't stop shedding (edge-case), scale admission service to 0 and route via emergency proxy path
Post-rollback: capture incident dump and run a focused runbook to identify mis-calibration parameters
monitoring_and_slo_impact: New metrics: admission.budget_used, admission.decisions.count, admission.fidelity_step.count, admission.rejections.count
Dashboards: per-region and per-tenant budget utilization and recent fidelity triggers
SLO considerations: aim to keep P0 tenants' error rate change <= 0.1% and P95 latency regressions <= +5ms during normal traffic
Alert: sustained rejections > 1% of requests for P0 tenants triggers paging and automatic rollback
risks_and_tradeoffs: Mis-estimated token cost can either over-shed or under-protect; we mitigate with short warm-up windows and conservative defaults
Extra hop at ingress increases median latency slightly; colocating service with proxy and optimizing codepath should keep it <1ms
Progressive fidelity may alter model outputs for some tenants — enterprise customers may require explicit opt-out
Centralized admission state introduces an availability dependency; we will design for local caching and degrade to probabilistic shedding if state is unreachable
